extracted.intended_audience: IP attorneys, patent litigators, corporate IP counsel, and parties budgeting for patent enforcement or defense
extracted.subtask_short: estimating patent litigation and IPR costs
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize and present median cost metrics for U.S. patent litigation and Inter Partes Review (IPR) by amount at risk, procedural stage, firm size, and service type to aid budgeting and decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Median costs of patent litigation by amount at risk and stage
rubrics_metrics.description: The Report shows the costs for four different amounts in controversy/at risk and for two stages, namely, through the end of discovery and through completion of the litigation (e.g., through trial and appeal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported median values (per AIPLA 2015 summary): Through discovery — <$1M at risk: $400K; $1M–$10M: $950K; $10M–$25M: $1.9M; >$25M: $3M. Through trial and appeal — <$1M: $600K; $1M–$10M: $2M; $10M–$25M: $3.1M; >$25M: $5M. Use these medians as planning benchmarks; actual costs may vary by firm size, venue, and case complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Median costs of Inter Partes Review (IPR) by procedural stage
rubrics_metrics.description: For the first time, the AIPLA Report includes the costs for Inter Partes Reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported median IPR costs: Through filing petition — $80K; Through end of motion practice — $200K; Through PTAB hearing — $275K; Through appeal — $350K. These are substantially lower than typical district-court litigation medians and can inform forum-selection and budget decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost components included in the Survey's litigation/IPR totals
rubrics_metrics.description: The costs are comprehensive and include outside and local counsel, associates, paralegal services, travel and living expenses, fees and costs for court reporters, copies, couriers, exhibit preparation, analytical testing, expert witnesses, translators, surveys, jury advisors, and similar expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When comparing or applying the medians, ensure your estimates include comparable line items (e.g., expert fees, travel, document preparation) because omission of these items will understate true costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Median hourly billing rates by firm size
rubrics_metrics.description: The Report points out median hourly billing rates for IP attorneys by firm size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported medians: large firms (101+ attorneys) — $437/hr; mid-sized firms (31+ attorneys) — $400/hr; smaller firms — $300–$350/hr. Expect lower overall matter costs for smaller firms partly due to these rate differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional litigation categories and venues for which the Report provides costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The AIPLA Report includes additional information about costs not presented here, for specific litigation types and venues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categories listed include: patent litigation in major metropolitan areas (including the DC area); litigation defending against suits by non-practicing entities (NPEs); ANDA/Hatch‑Waxman patent litigation; patent suits before the International Trade Commission under Section 337; copyright infringement litigation; trade secret litigation; trademark infringement litigation; and trademark opposition and cancellation proceedings. Use the category-specific medians for more precise budgeting when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical charges for patent-related legal services
rubrics_metrics.description: The Report further includes typical charges for various legal services for patents, trademarks and copyrights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For patents specifically, the Report lists charges for opinions of validity/invalidity, opinions of infringement/noninfringement, patentability searches, drafting, filing and prosecution of applications of various types and technologies, appeals to the Board, and ex parte re-exams. These per-service benchmarks help forecast prosecution and counseling costs beyond litigation/IPR.
